survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD country note is descriptive and does not provide an ILSA micro-dataset with student-level sampling weights or replicate-weight procedures. The figures and indicators are drawn from Education at a Glance 2025 and are reported as system-level statistics (e.g., unemployment rates by educational attainment, expenditure per student, teacher salary ratios, instruction time, class size). Because no student-level analysis dataset, weight variables, or complex survey design details are specified in the note, weighting cannot be applied or verified here. For any re-analysis using underlying microdata (not provided in this note), analysts should consult the corresponding Education at a Glance 2025 Sources, Methodologies and Technical Notes and the OECD Handbook for Internationally Comparative Education Statistics 2018 to identify the correct weighting and variance estimation approach for each indicator.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a country note that reports descriptive education-system indicators rather than estimating student-level cognitive achievement outcomes with plausible values. As a result, PV generation/combination and PV-specific missing-data procedures are not part of the analysis presented in the note. Missing-data handling is therefore not reported because the note does not describe any microdata imputation or PV estimation workflow.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The note does not define an analytic student sample or inclusion/exclusion criteria; it instead summarizes the latest available Education at a Glance 2025 indicators for Costa Rica. The underlying reference years and indicator-specific data sources are stated to be available in the corresponding tables and technical notes of Education at a Glance 2025.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD Education at a Glance 2025 country note for Costa Rica summarizes education-system characteristics using the latest available indicator data, with a thematic emphasis on tertiary education. It reports descriptive trends and comparisons across educational attainment groups (e.g., unemployment rates for 25–34 year-olds by attainment), labour-market associations (employment rates and wage gaps by attainment), and system inputs such as government expenditure per student by education level, teacher salary ratios, compulsory instruction time, school holidays, instructional time allocation to core subjects, and average class size. The note does not conduct student-level predictive modelling, does not specify an ILSA-style assessment instrument, and does not report plausible values or model performance metrics. Benchmarks are presented as OECD averages and cross-country ranges for each indicator, rather than as statistical model outputs. Methodological details for each indicator are deferred to the Education at a Glance 2025 Sources, Methodologies and Technical Notes.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is not an empirical ILSA microdata analysis paper; it is a descriptive OECD country note that aggregates indicator statistics for Costa Rica. Consequently, fields required for ML/predictive extraction (e.g., total student sample size, PV handling, missing-data imputation strategy, and model-based main findings) are not applicable or not reported in the note. The note also does not specify any student-level dataset, sampling frame, or weighting/replicate design, so ML-oriented methodological fields are intentionally left empty.
